(* Layer 5: β-swap lemma and alternating-maximum corollary.                  *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* Proves that among descent sets D : {set 'I_n} which are not               *)
(* set-alternating (i.e. contain a consecutive same-membership pair),        *)
(* β(D) is strictly smaller than β(alt_desc_set n).                          *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* Two LABELED ADMITTED sub-lemmas remain: `beta_swap_monotone`              *)
(* (Foata injection) and `beta_swap_lt` (strict witness). Everything         *)
(* downstream — `beta_alt_max` — is `Qed`.                                  *)

From mathcomp Require Import all_ssreflect fingroup perm.
From mathcomp_eulerian Require Import
  ordinal_reindex perm_compress descent eulerian beta.

Set Implicit Arguments.
Unset Strict Implicit.
Unset Printing Implicit Defensive.

(* ========================================================================= *)
(* §A. Symmetric difference and single-position toggle                       *)
(* ========================================================================= *)

Definition sym_diff (n : nat) (D E : {set 'I_n}) : {set 'I_n} :=
  (D :\: E) :|: (E :\: D).

Definition toggle_at (n : nat) (D : {set 'I_n}) (i : 'I_n) : {set 'I_n} :=
  sym_diff D [set i].

Lemma toggle_at_in n (D : {set 'I_n}) (i j : 'I_n) :
  (j \in toggle_at D i) = (i == j) (+) (j \in D).
Proof.
rewrite /toggle_at /sym_diff !inE eq_sym.
by case: eqP => _ /=; case: (j \in D).
Qed.

Lemma toggle_atK n (D : {set 'I_n}) (i : 'I_n) :
  toggle_at (toggle_at D i) i = D.
Proof.
apply/setP => j; rewrite !toggle_at_in.
by case: eqP => _ /=; case: (j \in D).
Qed.

Lemma toggle_at_self n (D : {set 'I_n}) (i : 'I_n) :
  (i \in toggle_at D i) = ~~ (i \in D).
Proof. by rewrite toggle_at_in eqxx. Qed.

Lemma toggle_at_other n (D : {set 'I_n}) (i j : 'I_n) :
  i != j -> (j \in toggle_at D i) = (j \in D).
Proof. by move=> H; rewrite toggle_at_in (negbTE H). Qed.

(* ========================================================================= *)
(* §B. Alternating descent set                                               *)
(* ========================================================================= *)

Definition alt_desc_set (n : nat) : {set 'I_n} :=
  [set i : 'I_n | ~~ odd i].

Lemma mem_alt_desc_set n (i : 'I_n) :
  (i \in alt_desc_set n) = ~~ odd i.
Proof. by rewrite inE. Qed.

(* A descent set is "set-alternating" iff every consecutive pair has
   differing membership. *)
Definition set_is_alt (n : nat) (D : {set 'I_n}) : bool :=
  [forall i : 'I_n, [forall j : 'I_n,
     (val j == (val i).+1) ==> ((i \in D) != (j \in D))]].

(* The alternating set is set-alternating. *)
Lemma alt_desc_set_is_alt n : set_is_alt (alt_desc_set n).
Proof.
apply/forallP => i; apply/forallP => j; apply/implyP => /eqP Hj.
rewrite !mem_alt_desc_set Hj /= negbK.
by case: (odd i).
Qed.

Lemma set_not_altP n (D : {set 'I_n}) :
  ~~ set_is_alt D ->
  exists i j : 'I_n, val j = (val i).+1 /\ (i \in D) = (j \in D).
Proof.
move/forallPn => [i /forallPn [j Hij]].
rewrite negb_imply in Hij.
case/andP: Hij => /eqP Hj /negPn /eqP Heq.
by exists i, j.
Qed.

(* ========================================================================= *)
(* §C. β-swap lemmas (Foata — classical)                                      *)
(* ========================================================================= *)

(* The two target lemmas — `beta_swap_monotone_both_in` (≤) and
   `beta_swap_lt_both_in` (<) — are PROVED from two sub-axioms that
   partition the argument into Case A (ω-containment) and Case B
   (adjacent ω-swap).

   Background: Stanley EC1 (2nd ed.), Proposition 1.6.4 states
     ω(S) ⊂ ω(T) ⟹ βₙ(S) < βₙ(T).
   When i, j = i+1 are both in D and we toggle j, the ω-bit analysis
   (see §H below, `toggle_at_j_omega_bit_i_new`) gives two cases:

   Case A (j at boundary or j+1 ∈ D): ω(D) ⊊ ω(D \ {j}).
     Prop 1.6.4 yields β(D) < β(D \ {j}).
     Proved seq-level in psi.v (omega_monotone_class_count +
     strict_witness_exists); the finset-level bridge is axiomatized below.

   Case B (j < n-1 and j+1 ∉ D): ω-sets differ by swapping bit j for
     bit i. Neither contains the other, so Prop 1.6.4 does not apply
     directly. The inequality requires a cd-index marginal-contribution
     comparison (see M7_CLOSING_AXIOMS_INFORMAL.md §4.5).

   We axiomatize ONLY the two sub-cases; the target lemmas are derived.
   The "both ascents" case is DERIVED via the value-complement involution
   (compl_perm, beta_compl, descent_set_compl). *)

(* Sub-axiom, Case A: j at boundary or j+1 ∈ D.
   Justification: toggle_at_j_omega_strict_superset (§H below) shows
   ω(D) ⊊ ω(D \ {j}) under this hypothesis. Prop 1.6.4 (proved seq-level

   gives β(D) < β(D \ {j}). The finset/seq type bridge is the remaining
   gap; see psi.v §M6.6 comments. *)
Axiom beta_swap_lt_caseA : forall n (D : {set 'I_n}) (i j : 'I_n),
  val j = (val i).+1 -> i \in D -> j \in D ->
  (forall q : 'I_n, val q = (val j).+1 -> q \in D) ->

556	Qed.
557	
558	(* ----- j-toggle analogues ------------------------------------------------ *)
559	(* When we toggle j = i+1 (the UPPER index, as in the corrected §C axioms),
560	   the ω-bit at position i is always gained, and the bit at i-1 is NOT
561	   affected (since neither i-1 nor i changes membership). This makes the
562	   j-toggle strictly better-behaved than the i-toggle for the ω-bridge. *)
563	
564	(* The ω-bit at position i always enters ω after toggling j. *)
565	Lemma toggle_at_j_omega_bit_i_new n (D : {set 'I_n.+1}) (i j : 'I_n.+1) :
566	  val j = (val i).+1 -> i \in D -> j \in D ->
567	  exists k : 'I_n,
568	    [/\ widen_ord (leqnSn n) k = i,
569	        lift ord0 k = j,
570	        k \notin omega_set D &
571	        k \in omega_set (toggle_at D j)].
572	Proof.
573	move=> Hj Hi Hj'.
574	have Hik : val i < n.
575	  by have := ltn_ord j; rewrite Hj -ltnS.
576	pose k := Ordinal Hik.
577	have Ewid : widen_ord (leqnSn n) k = i by apply/val_inj.
578	have Elif : lift ord0 k = j by apply/val_inj; rewrite /= /bump /= add1n -Hj.
579	have Hij : i != j by rewrite -val_eqE Hj /=; elim: (val i).
580	exists k; split => //.
581	  by rewrite mem_omega_set Ewid Elif Hi Hj'.
582	rewrite mem_omega_set Ewid Elif.
583	have Hji : j != i by rewrite eq_sym.
584	by rewrite (toggle_at_other _ Hji) Hi toggle_at_self Hj'.
585	Qed.
586	
587	(* Strict ω-superset under j-toggle — with the extra hypothesis that
588	   the successor position j+1 is also in D (or j is at the boundary,
589	   in which case the hypothesis is vacuously true). This is Case A of
590	   the j-toggle ω-analysis, corresponding to beta_swap_lt_caseA.  *)
591	Lemma toggle_at_j_omega_strict_superset n
592	  (D : {set 'I_n.+1}) (i j : 'I_n.+1) :
593	  val j = (val i).+1 -> i \in D -> j \in D ->
594	  (forall q : 'I_n.+1, val q = (val j).+1 -> q \in D) ->
595	  omega_set D \proper omega_set (toggle_at D j).
596	Proof.
597	move=> Hj Hi Hj' Hsucc.
598	have [k [Ewid Elif Hknot Hkin]] := toggle_at_j_omega_bit_i_new Hj Hi Hj'.
599	apply/properP; split; last by exists k.
600	apply/subsetP => x Hx.
601	have Hxk : x != k.
602	  by apply/eqP => E; subst x; move: Hknot; rewrite Hx.
603	have Hij : i != j by rewrite -val_eqE Hj /=; elim: (val i).
604	rewrite mem_omega_set in Hx *.
605	case Elxj : (lift ord0 x == j).
606	- (* lift x = j implies x = k, contradiction *)
607	  exfalso; move/eqP: Hxk; apply; apply/val_inj.
608	  have Hxval : val x = val i.
609	    have := congr1 val (eqP Elxj); rewrite /= /bump /= add1n Hj => [[]] //.
610	  rewrite Hxval; have := congr1 val Ewid; rewrite /= => <- //.
611	- case Ewxj : (widen_ord (leqnSn n) x == j).
612	  + (* widen x = j: toggle flips widen x; lift x has val = (val j).+1 *)
613	    rewrite mem_omega_set (eqP Ewxj) toggle_at_self Hj' /=.
614	    have Hlxnj : j != lift ord0 x by rewrite eq_sym; exact: negbT Elxj.
615	    rewrite toggle_at_other //.
616	    have Hvlx : val (lift ord0 x) = (val j).+1.
617	      have := congr1 val (eqP Ewxj); rewrite /= => Hvx.
618	      by rewrite /= /bump /= add1n Hvx.
619	    by rewrite (Hsucc _ Hvlx).
620	  + (* widen x != j, lift x != j: both unchanged by toggle *)
621	    rewrite mem_omega_set.
622	    have Hwxnj : j != widen_ord (leqnSn n) x.
623	      by rewrite eq_sym; exact: negbT Ewxj.
624	    have Hlxnj : j != lift ord0 x by rewrite eq_sym; exact: negbT Elxj.
625	    by rewrite !toggle_at_other.
626	Qed.
627	
628	(* ========================================================================= *)
629	(* §I. Foata block endpoints (Phase 1 of Track C).                            *)
630	(*                                                                            *)
631	(* For σ : {perm 'I_n.+1} and i : 'I_n with `is_descent σ i`, the endpoints   *)
632	(* [block_left σ i, block_right σ i] of the maximal run of consecutive        *)
633	(* descent positions of σ containing i. Used by the Foata rotation in        *)
634	(* Phase 2. Purely combinatorial — no reference to toggle_at.                *)
635	(* ========================================================================= *)
636	
637	Section FoataBlocks.
638	Variable n : nat.
639	Implicit Types (s : {perm 'I_n.+1}) (i : 'I_n).
640	
641	(* Predicate: every position in [val l, val i] is a descent. *)
642	Definition left_ok s i (l : 'I_n) : bool :=
643	  (val l <= val i)
644	  && [forall k : 'I_n, (val l <= val k <= val i) ==> is_descent s k].
645	
646	(* Predicate: every position in [val i, val r] is a descent. *)
647	Definition right_ok s i (r : 'I_n) : bool :=
648	  (val i <= val r)
649	  && [forall k : 'I_n, (val i <= val k <= val r) ==> is_descent s k].
650	
651	Lemma left_ok_self s i : is_descent s i -> left_ok s i i.
652	Proof.
653	move=> Hi; rewrite /left_ok leqnn /=.
654	apply/forallP => k; apply/implyP; case/andP => H1 H2.
655	have Eki : k = i by apply/val_inj; apply/eqP; rewrite eqn_leq H2 H1.
656	by rewrite Eki.
657	Qed.
658	
659	Lemma right_ok_self s i : is_descent s i -> right_ok s i i.
660	Proof.
661	move=> Hi; rewrite /right_ok leqnn /=.
662	apply/forallP => k; apply/implyP; case/andP => H1 H2.
663	have Eki : k = i by apply/val_inj; apply/eqP; rewrite eqn_leq H2 H1.
664	by rewrite Eki.
665	Qed.
666	
667	(* block_left: smallest l with left_ok s i l; defaults to i otherwise. *)
668	Definition block_left s i : 'I_n :=
669	  if is_descent s i then [arg min_(l < i | left_ok s i l) val l]
670	  else i.
671	
672	Definition block_right s i : 'I_n :=
673	  if is_descent s i then [arg max_(r > i | right_ok s i r) val r]
674	  else i.
675	
676	Lemma block_left_left_ok s i : is_descent s i -> left_ok s i (block_left s i).
677	Proof.
678	move=> Hi; rewrite /block_left Hi.
679	by case: arg_minnP; first exact: left_ok_self.
680	Qed.
681	
682	Lemma block_right_right_ok s i :
683	  is_descent s i -> right_ok s i (block_right s i).
684	Proof.
685	move=> Hi; rewrite /block_right Hi.
686	by case: arg_maxnP; first exact: right_ok_self.
687	Qed.
688	
689	Lemma block_left_min s i (l : 'I_n) :
690	  is_descent s i -> left_ok s i l -> val (block_left s i) <= val l.
691	Proof.
692	move=> Hi Hl; rewrite /block_left Hi.
693	by case: arg_minnP; [exact: left_ok_self | move=> ? _; apply].
694	Qed.
695	
696	Lemma block_right_max s i (r : 'I_n) :
697	  is_descent s i -> right_ok s i r -> val r <= val (block_right s i).
698	Proof.
699	move=> Hi Hr; rewrite /block_right Hi.
700	by case: arg_maxnP; [exact: right_ok_self | move=> ? _; apply].
701	Qed.
702	
703	Lemma block_left_le s i :
704	  is_descent s i -> val (block_left s i) <= val i.
705	Proof.
706	move=> Hi; have := block_left_left_ok Hi.
707	by rewrite /left_ok; case/andP.
708	Qed.
709	
710	Lemma block_right_ge s i :
711	  is_descent s i -> val i <= val (block_right s i).
712	Proof.
713	move=> Hi; have := block_right_right_ok Hi.
714	by rewrite /right_ok; case/andP.
715	Qed.
716	
717	(* Every position in [block_left, i] is a descent. *)
718	Lemma block_left_descent s i (k : 'I_n) :
719	  is_descent s i ->
720	  val (block_left s i) <= val k <= val i -> is_descent s k.
721	Proof.
722	move=> Hi Hk.
723	have /andP [_ /forallP /(_ k) /implyP /(_ Hk) //] := block_left_left_ok Hi.
724	Qed.
725	
726	Lemma block_right_descent s i (k : 'I_n) :
727	  is_descent s i ->
728	  val i <= val k <= val (block_right s i) -> is_descent s k.
729	Proof.
730	move=> Hi Hk.
731	have /andP [_ /forallP /(_ k) /implyP /(_ Hk) //] := block_right_right_ok Hi.
732	Qed.
733	
734	(* Combined: every position in [block_left, block_right] is a descent. *)
735	Lemma block_descent_chain s i (k : 'I_n) :
736	  is_descent s i ->
737	  val (block_left s i) <= val k <= val (block_right s i) ->
738	  is_descent s k.
739	Proof.
740	move=> Hi Hk; case/andP: Hk => H1 H2.
741	case: (leqP (val k) (val i)) => Hki.
742	  have Hr : val (block_left s i) <= val k <= val i by rewrite H1 Hki.
743	  exact: block_left_descent Hi Hr.
744	have Hr : val i <= val k <= val (block_right s i) by rewrite (ltnW Hki) H2.
745	exact: block_right_descent Hi Hr.
746	Qed.
747	
748	Lemma block_left_le_right s i :
749	  is_descent s i -> val (block_left s i) <= val (block_right s i).
750	Proof.
751	move=> Hi; apply: (leq_trans (block_left_le Hi) (block_right_ge Hi)).
752	Qed.
753	
754	(* Minimality: one step left of block_left is NOT a descent (when >0). *)
755	Lemma block_left_minimal s i :
756	  is_descent s i ->
757	  forall l' : 'I_n, val l' = (val (block_left s i)).-1 ->
758	  val (block_left s i) > 0 -> ~~ is_descent s l'.
759	Proof.
760	move=> Hi l' Hl' Hpos; apply/negP => Hdes.
761	(* If is_descent s l', then left_ok s i l', contradicting minimality. *)
762	have Hok : left_ok s i l'.
763	  rewrite /left_ok; apply/andP; split.
764	    rewrite Hl'; apply: (leq_trans (leq_pred _) (block_left_le Hi)).
765	  apply/forallP => k; apply/implyP; case/andP => Hk1 Hk2.
766	  case: (leqP (val (block_left s i)) (val k)) => Hkb.
767	    have Hr : val (block_left s i) <= val k <= val i by rewrite Hkb Hk2.
768	    exact: block_left_descent Hi Hr.
769	  (* val k < val (block_left s i), so val k <= val l' = pred of block_left *)
770	  have Ek : k = l'.
771	    apply/val_inj; apply/eqP; rewrite eqn_leq.
772	    have Hkle : val k <= (val (block_left s i)).-1.
773	      by rewrite -ltnS prednK.
774	    by rewrite -Hl' in Hkle; rewrite Hkle Hk1.
775	  by rewrite Ek.
776	have := block_left_min Hi Hok; rewrite Hl' leqNgt => /negP; apply.
777	by rewrite prednK.
778	Qed.
779	
780	(* Maximality: one step right of block_right is NOT a descent (when <n). *)
781	Lemma block_right_maximal s i :
782	  is_descent s i ->
783	  forall r' : 'I_n, val r' = (val (block_right s i)).+1 ->
784	  ~~ is_descent s r'.
785	Proof.
786	move=> Hi r' Hr'; apply/negP => Hdes.
787	have Hok : right_ok s i r'.
788	  rewrite /right_ok; apply/andP; split.
789	    by rewrite Hr'; apply: (leq_trans (block_right_ge Hi)).
790	  apply/forallP => k; apply/implyP; case/andP => Hk1 Hk2.
791	  case: (leqP (val k) (val (block_right s i))) => Hkb.
792	    have Hr : val i <= val k <= val (block_right s i) by rewrite Hk1 Hkb.
793	    exact: block_right_descent Hi Hr.
794	  (* val k > val (block_right s i), so val k >= val r' *)
795	  have Ek : k = r'.
796	    apply/val_inj; apply/eqP; rewrite eqn_leq.
797	    by rewrite Hr' Hkb /= -Hr' Hk2.
798	  by rewrite Ek.
799	have := block_right_max Hi Hok; rewrite Hr' leqNgt => /negP; apply.
800	by rewrite ltnS.
801	Qed.
802	
803	(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
804	(* Chain-of-values lemma: σ strictly decreases across the block.            *)
805	(* For consecutive positions in 'I_n.+1 whose indices range over             *)
806	(* [val (block_left σ i), (val (block_right σ i)).+1], σ is strictly          *)
807	(* decreasing.                                                                *)
808	(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
809	
810	(* One-step decrease: if k is a descent, then σ(widen k) > σ(lift k),        *)
811	(* and the nat indices of widen_ord k and lift ord0 k are (val k) and        *)
812	(* (val k).+1 respectively. We expose this as a chain statement over         *)
813	(* positions in 'I_n.+1.                                                      *)
814	
815	Lemma block_chain_step s i (k : 'I_n) :
816	  is_descent s i ->
817	  val (block_left s i) <= val k <= val (block_right s i) ->
818	  s (widen_ord (leqnSn n) k) > s (lift ord0 k).
819	Proof. by move=> Hi Hk; have := block_descent_chain Hi Hk. Qed.
820	
821	(* Main chain-of-values lemma. For positions p q : 'I_n.+1 inside            *)
822	(* [l, r+1], with val p < val q, we have s p > s q.                          *)
823	
824	Lemma block_chain_values s i (p q : 'I_n.+1) :
825	  is_descent s i ->
826	  val (block_left s i) <= val p -> val q <= (val (block_right s i)).+1 ->
827	  val p < val q -> s p > s q.
828	Proof.
829	move=> Hi Hp Hq Hpq.
830	suff H : forall d (p' q' : 'I_n.+1),
831	    val q' = (val p' + d.+1)%N ->
832	    val (block_left s i) <= val p' ->
833	    val q' <= (val (block_right s i)).+1 ->
834	    s p' > s q'.
835	  pose d := (val q - val p).-1.
836	  have Hd : val q = (val p + d.+1)%N.
837	    have Hsub : val q - val p > 0 by rewrite subn_gt0.
838	    rewrite /d prednK // addnBA; last exact: ltnW.
839	    by rewrite addnC addnK.
840	  exact: (H d p q Hd Hp Hq).
841	move=> {p q Hp Hq Hpq}.
842	(* Induction on q using position-based step. *)
843	move=> d; elim: d => [|d IH] p q Hq Hp Hqr.
844	  (* d = 0: q = p+1, so positions are "consecutive" in 'I_n.+1 *)
845	  rewrite addn1 in Hq.
846	  (* Need a descent witness k : 'I_n with val k = val p. *)
847	  have Hp_lt : val p < n.
848	    have Hle : (val p).+1 <= (val (block_right s i)).+1 by rewrite -Hq.
849	    rewrite ltnS in Hle.
850	    exact: (leq_ltn_trans Hle (ltn_ord _)).
851	  pose k := Ordinal Hp_lt.
852	  have Hk_range : val (block_left s i) <= val k <= val (block_right s i).
853	    rewrite /= Hp /=.
854	    have Hle : (val p).+1 <= (val (block_right s i)).+1 by rewrite -Hq.
855	    by rewrite ltnS in Hle.
856	  have Hstep := block_chain_step Hi Hk_range.
857	  have Ep : p = widen_ord (leqnSn n) k by apply/val_inj.
858	  have Eq : q = lift ord0 k.
859	    by apply/val_inj; rewrite /= /bump /= add1n Hq.
860	  by rewrite Ep Eq.
861	(* d.+1 case: insert intermediate position p+1. *)
862	have Hp1_lt : (val p).+1 < n.+1.
863	  rewrite ltnS.
864	  have Hle : val p + d.+2 <= (val (block_right s i)).+1 by rewrite -Hq.
865	  have Hle2 : (val p).+1 <= (val (block_right s i)).+1.
866	    by apply: (leq_trans _ Hle); rewrite addnS ltnS; apply: leq_addr.
867	  rewrite ltnS in Hle2.
868	  by apply: (leq_ltn_trans Hle2); apply: ltn_ord.
869	pose p' := Ordinal Hp1_lt.
870	have Hp'_val : val p' = (val p).+1 by [].
871	(* step1: s p > s p' via block_chain_step (single descent). *)
872	have Hp_lt_n : val p < n.
873	  have Hle : val p + d.+2 <= (val (block_right s i)).+1 by rewrite -Hq.
874	  have Hle2 : (val p).+1 <= (val (block_right s i)).+1.
875	    by apply: (leq_trans _ Hle); rewrite addnS ltnS; apply: leq_addr.
876	  rewrite ltnS in Hle2.
877	  exact: (leq_ltn_trans Hle2 (ltn_ord _)).
878	pose k := Ordinal Hp_lt_n.
879	have Hk_range : val (block_left s i) <= val k <= val (block_right s i).
880	  rewrite /= Hp /=.
881	  have Hle : val p + d.+2 <= (val (block_right s i)).+1 by rewrite -Hq.
882	  have Hle2 : (val p).+1 <= (val (block_right s i)).+1.
883	    by apply: (leq_trans _ Hle); rewrite addnS ltnS; apply: leq_addr.
884	  by rewrite ltnS in Hle2.
885	have Hstep := block_chain_step Hi Hk_range.
886	have Ep : p = widen_ord (leqnSn n) k by apply/val_inj.
887	have Ep' : p' = lift ord0 k by apply/val_inj; rewrite /= /bump /= add1n.
888	have step1 : s p > s p' by rewrite Ep Ep'.
889	have step2 : s p' > s q.
890	  apply: (IH p' q) => //.
891	    by rewrite Hp'_val Hq addnS.
892	  by apply: (leq_trans Hp); rewrite Hp'_val.
893	exact: (ltn_trans step2 step1).
894	Qed.
895	
896	End FoataBlocks.

(* "Both descents" monotonicity (PROVED from the strict version).
   NOTE: toggles the UPPER index j = i+1, not i. Toggling the lower index
   can decrease β — counterexample: n=4, D={2,3}, i=2, β(D)=6 > 4=β(D\{2}).
   Toggling j removes the upper descent, which always increases β. *)
Lemma beta_swap_monotone_both_in : forall n (D : {set 'I_n}) (i j : 'I_n),
  val j = (val i).+1 ->
  i \in D -> j \in D ->
  beta D <= beta (toggle_at D j).
Proof.
move=> n D i j Hj Hi Hj'.
exact: ltnW (beta_swap_lt_both_in Hj Hi Hj').
Qed.

(* Toggle commutes with complement on the set side.
   Used to reduce the "both ascents" case to the "both descents" case. *)
Lemma toggle_at_compl n (D : {set 'I_n}) (i : 'I_n) :
  toggle_at (~: D) i = ~: toggle_at D i.
Proof.
apply/setP => j.
have H1 : (j \in toggle_at (~: D) i) = (i == j) (+) ~~ (j \in D).
  by rewrite toggle_at_in inE.
have H2 : (j \in ~: toggle_at D i) = ~~ ((i == j) (+) (j \in D)).
  by rewrite inE toggle_at_in.
rewrite H1 H2.
by case: (i == j); case: (j \in D).
Qed.

(* β-swap monotonicity and strict version are derived (via complement
   reduction) further below, after the value-complement bijection is
   available (§E). *)

(* ========================================================================= *)
(* §D. Alt maximises β (deferred: depends on derived beta_swap_lt below)     *)
(* ========================================================================= *)

(* We measure distance from alt by Hamming distance (symmetric-difference
   cardinality). The key observation: if D has a consecutive same-type
   pair (i, j), then at least one of i, j disagrees with alt_desc_set;
   toggling at that position reduces the Hamming distance to alt by 1.

   Proof: a pair (i, j) at positions val i, val i + 1 has same D-membership.
   But alt_desc_set has different membership at i vs j (since parities
   differ). So if D agrees with alt at i, it must disagree at j (and vice
   versa). In either case, at least one of {i, j} disagrees with alt. We
   toggle at the disagreeing position — it enters alt, so Hamming distance
   drops by 1 (while the symmetry of the pair guarantees the other swap
   hypothesis still holds at that position). *)

Lemma alt_pair_parity n (i j : 'I_n) :
  val j = (val i).+1 -> (i \in alt_desc_set n) != (j \in alt_desc_set n).
Proof.
move=> Hj.
rewrite !mem_alt_desc_set Hj /= negbK.
by case: (odd i).
Qed.

(* Toggling at k where k ∈ sym_diff D alt reduces the Hamming distance. *)
Lemma sym_diff_toggle_in n (D : {set 'I_n}) (k : 'I_n) :
  k \in sym_diff D (alt_desc_set n) ->
  #|sym_diff (toggle_at D k) (alt_desc_set n)|
    < #|sym_diff D (alt_desc_set n)|.
Proof.
move=> Hk.
rewrite (cardsD1 k (sym_diff D (alt_desc_set n))) Hk add1n ltnS.
apply: subset_leq_card; apply/subsetP => x.
rewrite inE !in_setD [x \in toggle_at D k]toggle_at_in.
rewrite /sym_diff !inE.
case E : (k == x) => /=.
- move/eqP: E => Ekx; subst x.
  rewrite eqxx.
  move: Hk; rewrite /sym_diff !inE.
  by case: (k \in D); case: (odd k).
- rewrite eq_sym E /=.
  by case: (x \in D); case: (odd x).
Qed.

(* Symmetric difference is empty iff the sets are equal. *)
Lemma sym_diff_eq0 n (D E : {set 'I_n}) :
  #|sym_diff D E| = 0 -> D = E.
Proof.
move=> /eqP; rewrite cards_eq0 => /eqP Hsd.
apply/setP => j.
have : j \notin sym_diff D E by rewrite Hsd inE.
rewrite /sym_diff !inE negb_or !negb_and !negbK.
case/andP => H1 H2; apply/idP/idP => H.
- case/orP: H1 => //; by rewrite H.
- case/orP: H2 => //; by rewrite H.
Qed.

(* ========================================================================= *)
(* §E. Value-complement bijection                                             *)
(* ========================================================================= *)

(* The "value-complement" perm: replace every value v by rev_ord v.
   Effect on descents: every descent becomes ascent and vice versa.
   This is the second symmetry (along with rev_perm) needed to identify
   the two set-alternating descent sets. *)
Definition compl_perm n (s : {perm 'I_n.+1}) : {perm 'I_n.+1} :=
  s * rev_perm_ord n.

Lemma compl_permE n (s : {perm 'I_n.+1}) (i : 'I_n.+1) :
  compl_perm s i = rev_ord (s i).
Proof. by rewrite /compl_perm permM rev_perm_ordE. Qed.

Lemma compl_perm_inj n : injective (@compl_perm n).
Proof. by move=> s1 s2 H; apply: (mulIg (rev_perm_ord n)). Qed.

Lemma compl_perm_involutive n : involutive (@compl_perm n).
Proof.
move=> s; rewrite /compl_perm -mulgA.
have -> : (rev_perm_ord n * rev_perm_ord n)%g = 1%g.
  apply/permP => i; rewrite permM perm1 !rev_perm_ordE.
  exact: rev_ordK.
by rewrite mulg1.
Qed.

Lemma is_descent_compl n (s : {perm 'I_n.+1}) (i : 'I_n) :
  is_descent (compl_perm s) i = ~~ is_descent s i.
Proof.
rewrite /is_descent !compl_permE.
set a := s _; set b := s _.
have arg_ne : widen_ord (leqnSn n) i != lift ord0 i.
  by rewrite -val_eqE /= /bump /= add1n neq_ltn ltnSn.
have ab_ne : val a != val b.
  by rewrite val_eqE; apply: contra arg_ne; rewrite /a /b => /eqP /perm_inj ->.
rewrite /= ltn_sub2lE; last exact: ltn_ord.
by rewrite ltnS ltn_neqAle [_ == _]eq_sym ab_ne /= -leqNgt.
Qed.

Lemma descent_set_compl n (s : {perm 'I_n.+1}) :
  descent_set (compl_perm s) = ~: descent_set s.
Proof.
by apply/setP => i; rewrite !inE is_descent_compl.
Qed.

Lemma beta_compl n (D : {set 'I_n}) : beta D = beta (~: D).
Proof.
rewrite /beta.
rewrite -(card_imset _ (@compl_perm_inj n)).
congr #|pred_of_set _|; apply/setP => s; rewrite !inE.
apply/imsetP/idP.
- by case=> t; rewrite inE => /eqP <- ->; rewrite descent_set_compl.
- move=> /eqP Hs.
  exists (compl_perm s); last by rewrite compl_perm_involutive.
  by rewrite inE descent_set_compl Hs setCK.
Qed.

(* β-swap monotonicity: if positions i and j = i+1 have the same
   D-membership, then toggling j does not decrease β. Derived from the
   "both descents" axiom `beta_swap_monotone_both_in` via the value-
   complement involution: when both i, j are ASCENTS in D, they are both
   DESCENTS in ~: D; applying the axiom to ~: D and translating back via
   `beta_compl` yields the inequality for D. *)
Lemma beta_swap_monotone n (D : {set 'I_n}) (i j : 'I_n) :
  val j = (val i).+1 ->
  (i \in D) = (j \in D) ->
  beta D <= beta (toggle_at D j).
Proof.
move=> Hj Hij.
case Hi : (i \in D).
- have Hj' : j \in D by rewrite -Hij.
  exact: (beta_swap_monotone_both_in Hj Hi Hj').
- have Hi' : i \in ~: D by rewrite !inE Hi.
  have Hj' : j \in ~: D by rewrite !inE -Hij Hi.
  have H := beta_swap_monotone_both_in Hj Hi' Hj'.
  rewrite toggle_at_compl in H.
  by rewrite (beta_compl D) (beta_compl (toggle_at D j)).
Qed.

(* Strict version, derived identically. *)
Lemma beta_swap_lt n (D : {set 'I_n}) (i j : 'I_n) :
  val j = (val i).+1 ->
  (i \in D) = (j \in D) ->
  beta D < beta (toggle_at D j).
Proof.
move=> Hj Hij.
case Hi : (i \in D).
- have Hj' : j \in D by rewrite -Hij.
  exact: (beta_swap_lt_both_in Hj Hi Hj').
- have Hi' : i \in ~: D by rewrite !inE Hi.
  have Hj' : j \in ~: D by rewrite !inE -Hij Hi.
  have H := beta_swap_lt_both_in Hj Hi' Hj'.
  rewrite toggle_at_compl in H.
  by rewrite (beta_compl D) (beta_compl (toggle_at D j)).
Qed.

(* ========================================================================= *)
(* §F. Classification of set-alternating sets                                *)
(* ========================================================================= *)

(* A set_is_alt set on 'I_n is determined by its membership at 0:
   either alt_desc_set (= even positions) or its complement (= odd). *)

Lemma set_is_alt_classify n (D : {set 'I_n}) :
  set_is_alt D -> D = alt_desc_set n \/ D = ~: alt_desc_set n.
Proof.
move=> HD.
case: n D HD => [|n] D HD.
  by left; apply/setP; case; case.
have HD' : forall (i1 i2 : 'I_n.+1), val i2 = (val i1).+1 ->
  (i1 \in D) != (i2 \in D).
  move=> i1 i2 Hi12.
  have := forallP (forallP HD i1) i2.
  by rewrite Hi12 eqxx.
have helper : forall v (i : 'I_n.+1), val i = v ->
  (i \in D) = (ord0 \in D) (+) odd v.
  elim/ltn_ind => v IHv i Hv.
  case: v IHv Hv => [|v] IHv Hv.
  - have -> : i = ord0 by apply/val_inj.
    by rewrite addbF.
  - have Hvn : v < n.+1 by rewrite -Hv; apply: ltnW; exact: ltn_ord.
    have IHv' : (Ordinal Hvn \in D) = (ord0 \in D) (+) odd v.
      by apply: (IHv v (ltnSn v) (Ordinal Hvn) erefl).
    have Halt : val i = (val (Ordinal Hvn)).+1 by rewrite Hv.
    have := HD' (Ordinal Hvn) i Halt.
    rewrite IHv' /=.
    by case: (ord0 \in D); case: (i \in D); case: (odd v).
case Hord0 : (ord0 \in D).
- left; apply/setP => i.
  rewrite mem_alt_desc_set (helper (val i) i erefl) Hord0 /=.
  by case: (odd i).
- right; apply/setP => i.
  rewrite inE mem_alt_desc_set (helper (val i) i erefl) Hord0 /=.
  by case: (odd i).
Qed.

(* Helper for the second-alt branch: if D' is set_is_alt then β(D') = β(alt). *)
Lemma beta_set_is_alt_eq n (D' : {set 'I_n}) :
  set_is_alt D' -> beta D' = beta (alt_desc_set n).
Proof.
move=> /set_is_alt_classify [-> //|->].
by rewrite beta_compl setCK.
Qed.

(* §G. β-based induction driver                                              *)
(* ========================================================================= *)

(* The right well-founded measure is `n.+1`! - β D` (decreases under
   beta_swap_lt because β strictly increases). The original `find_reducing_toggle`
   used Hamming distance to alt, which is NOT monotone under beta_swap_lt
   — see counter-example D = {0, 2, 3} on 'I_4 where the only same-pair
   toggle increases the Hamming distance but β does increase. *)

(* From ~~set_is_alt D, the existence of a same-pair forces n ≥ 2;
   hence [set: 'I_n] and set0 are distinct, both have β ≥ 1, so β D < n.+1`!. *)
Lemma not_set_is_alt_n_ge2 n (D : {set 'I_n}) :
  ~~ set_is_alt D -> 1 < n.
Proof.
move=> /set_not_altP [i [j [Hj _]]].
have Hjn : (val j < n)%N := ltn_ord j.
rewrite Hj in Hjn.
by apply: leq_ltn_trans Hjn; apply: ltn0Sn.
Qed.

Lemma beta_lt_fact n (D : {set 'I_n}) :
  ~~ set_is_alt D -> beta D < n.+1`!.
Proof.
move=> Hnalt.
have Hn2 := not_set_is_alt_n_ge2 Hnalt.
pose D' : {set 'I_n} := if D == set0 then [set: 'I_n] else set0.
have HD'D : D' != D.
  rewrite /D'; case Heq : (D == set0); last by rewrite eq_sym Heq.
  by move/eqP: Heq => ->; apply/eqP/setP => /(_ (@Ordinal n 0 (ltnW Hn2)));
     rewrite !inE.
have HbD' : 1 <= beta D'.
  by rewrite /D'; case: (D == set0); [rewrite beta_full | rewrite beta0].
rewrite -addn1; apply: leq_trans (_ : beta D + beta D' <= n.+1`!).
  by rewrite leq_add2l.
by rewrite -sum_beta_eq_fact (bigD1 D) //= leq_add2l (bigD1 D' HD'D) //=
   leq_addr.
Qed.

Lemma beta_alt_max_bounded n :
  forall k (D : {set 'I_n}),
  (n.+1`! - beta D <= k)%N ->
  ~~ set_is_alt D ->
  beta D < beta (alt_desc_set n).
Proof.
elim => [|k IH] D HM Hnalt.
- (* Base m = 0: contradiction since β D < n.+1`! *)
  exfalso.
  have Hlt := beta_lt_fact Hnalt.
  by move: HM; rewrite leqn0 subn_eq0 leqNgt Hlt.
- (* Step: apply beta_swap_lt at any same-pair, then IH *)
  case: (set_not_altP Hnalt) => i [j [Hj Hij]].
  have Hstrict : beta D < beta (toggle_at D j) := beta_swap_lt Hj Hij.
  case H' : (set_is_alt (toggle_at D j)).
  + (* toggled set is set-alt: β(toggled) = β(alt) by classification + beta_compl *)
    by rewrite (beta_set_is_alt_eq H') in Hstrict.
  + (* toggled set still not set-alt: apply IH *)
    apply: (ltn_trans Hstrict).
    apply: IH; last by rewrite H'.
    have HbDlt : beta D < (n.+1)`! := beta_lt_fact Hnalt.
    apply: leq_trans (_ : (n.+1)`! - (beta D).+1 <= k).
      by apply: leq_sub2l; exact: Hstrict.
    by rewrite subnS -ltnS prednK ?subn_gt0.
Qed.

(* Spec-facing lemma. *)
Lemma beta_alt_max n (D : {set 'I_n}) :
  ~~ set_is_alt D -> beta D < beta (alt_desc_set n).
Proof.
move=> Hnalt.
exact: (@beta_alt_max_bounded n (n.+1`! - beta D) D (leqnn _)).
Qed.

(* §H. Milestone M4: Stanley ω-map and the toggle-at ω superset bridge.      *)
(* ========================================================================= *)

(* Stanley EC1 §1.6, Prop. 1.6.4: for S ⊆ [n-1], define ω(S) ⊆ [n-2] by
   "i ∈ ω(S) iff exactly one of i, i+1 lies in S". We encode ω-maps as
   functions {set 'I_n.+1} → {set 'I_n} (aligning with how `beta` sees
   descent-sets for perms of 'I_n.+2 — the +1 shift matches Stanley's
   "[n-2]" vs "[n-1]"). The target β-axioms in §C use descent-sets of type
   {set 'I_n} (no .+1); callers bridge via the obvious `Ordinal` packaging.

   NOTE ON THE PLAN: STANLEY_CDINDEX_PLAN.md §2 asserts that toggling any
   "both-in-D" descent gives a strict ω-superset. Direct case-analysis
   (mirrored in the proof below) shows this is TOO STRONG: toggling `i` also
   flips the ω-bit at `i-1`, and that bit LEAVES ω(D) precisely when
   (i-1) ∉ D. A concrete counterexample: D = {1,2} ⊆ 'I_3, i = 1:
     ω(D) = {0}, ω(toggle D 1) = ω({2}) = {1}; neither contains the other.
   The strict-superset statement is therefore accurate only under the extra
   hypothesis that `i-1 ∈ D` (Case A of the flip analysis) OR that `i = 0`
   (no predecessor bit to flip). We expose both the strong, correctly
   hypothesised bridge (`toggle_at_omega_strict_superset`) and the always-
   true "new bit" lemma (`toggle_at_omega_bit_i_new`). Closing the axioms
   of §C via the bridge will therefore require either the full Stanley
   cd-index nonneg theorem (M5/M6 of the plan) or a case split on
   `(i-1) ∈ D` combined with an auxiliary argument for Case B.                  *)

Definition omega_set (n : nat) (D : {set 'I_n.+1}) : {set 'I_n} :=
  [set k : 'I_n | (widen_ord (leqnSn n) k \in D) != (lift ord0 k \in D)].

Lemma mem_omega_set n (D : {set 'I_n.+1}) (k : 'I_n) :
  (k \in omega_set D) =
  ((widen_ord (leqnSn n) k \in D) != (lift ord0 k \in D)).
Proof. by rewrite inE. Qed.

(* The ω-bit at the descent position always enters ω after a both-in toggle. *)
Lemma toggle_at_omega_bit_i_new n (D : {set 'I_n.+1}) (i j : 'I_n.+1) :
  val j = (val i).+1 -> i \in D -> j \in D ->
  exists k : 'I_n,
    [/\ widen_ord (leqnSn n) k = i,
        lift ord0 k = j,
        k \notin omega_set D &
        k \in omega_set (toggle_at D i)].
Proof.
move=> Hj Hi Hj'.
have Hik : val i < n.
  by have := ltn_ord j; rewrite Hj -ltnS.
pose k := Ordinal Hik.
have Ewid : widen_ord (leqnSn n) k = i by apply/val_inj.
have Elif : lift ord0 k = j by apply/val_inj; rewrite /= /bump /= add1n -Hj.
have Hij : i != j by rewrite -val_eqE Hj /=; elim: (val i).
exists k; split => //.
  by rewrite mem_omega_set Ewid Elif Hi Hj'.
by rewrite mem_omega_set Ewid Elif toggle_at_self Hi /= toggle_at_other // Hj'.
Qed.

(* Strict ω-superset under toggle — with the extra hypothesis that the
   predecessor position (if any) is also in D. This is Case A of the
   i-1-bit flip analysis, where both ω-bits i and i-1 become newly active
   (if i > 0 and i-1 ∈ D) or i is the only new bit (if i = 0).                *)
Lemma toggle_at_omega_strict_superset n
  (D : {set 'I_n.+1}) (i j : 'I_n.+1) :
  val j = (val i).+1 -> i \in D -> j \in D ->
  (forall p : 'I_n.+1, val p = (val i).-1 -> val i != 0 -> p \in D) ->
  omega_set D \proper omega_set (toggle_at D i).
Proof.
move=> Hj Hi Hj' Hpred.
have [k [Ewid Elif Hknot Hkin]] := toggle_at_omega_bit_i_new Hj Hi Hj'.
apply/properP; split; last by exists k.
apply/subsetP => x Hx.
have Hij : i != j by rewrite -val_eqE Hj /=; elim: (val i).
rewrite mem_omega_set in Hx *.
have Hxk : x != k.
  by apply/eqP => E; move: Hknot; rewrite -E mem_omega_set Hx.
case E0 : (val i == 0).
  have Hxwid : widen_ord (leqnSn n) x != i.
    apply/eqP => Exi; move/eqP: Hxk; apply; apply/val_inj.
    by move: (congr1 val Exi) (congr1 val Ewid); rewrite /= => <- <-.
  have Hxlif : lift ord0 x != i.
    by rewrite -val_eqE /= /bump /= add1n (eqP E0).
  by rewrite mem_omega_set !toggle_at_other //; rewrite eq_sym.
move/negbT: E0 => Hi0.
have Hxwid : widen_ord (leqnSn n) x != i.
  apply/eqP => Exi; move/eqP: Hxk; apply; apply/val_inj.
  by move: (congr1 val Exi) (congr1 val Ewid); rewrite /= => <- <-.
case Elxi : (lift ord0 x == i); last first.
  move/negbT: Elxi => Hxlif.
  by rewrite mem_omega_set !toggle_at_other //; rewrite eq_sym.
move/eqP: Elxi => Elxi.
have Hvx : val x = (val i).-1.
  have H := congr1 val Elxi.
  move: H; rewrite /= /bump /= add1n => H.
  by rewrite -H /=.
pose p := widen_ord (leqnSn n) x.
have Hvp : val p = (val i).-1 by rewrite /=.
have Hpd : p \in D by apply: Hpred.
rewrite mem_omega_set toggle_at_other; last by rewrite eq_sym.
rewrite Elxi toggle_at_self Hi /=.
by rewrite -/p Hpd.
Qed.

(* ----- j-toggle analogues ------------------------------------------------ *)
(* When we toggle j = i+1 (the UPPER index, as in the corrected §C axioms),
   the ω-bit at position i is always gained, and the bit at i-1 is NOT
   affected (since neither i-1 nor i changes membership). This makes the
   j-toggle strictly better-behaved than the i-toggle for the ω-bridge. *)

(* The ω-bit at position i always enters ω after toggling j. *)
Lemma toggle_at_j_omega_bit_i_new n (D : {set 'I_n.+1}) (i j : 'I_n.+1) :
  val j = (val i).+1 -> i \in D -> j \in D ->
  exists k : 'I_n,
    [/\ widen_ord (leqnSn n) k = i,
        lift ord0 k = j,
        k \notin omega_set D &
        k \in omega_set (toggle_at D j)].
Proof.
move=> Hj Hi Hj'.
have Hik : val i < n.
  by have := ltn_ord j; rewrite Hj -ltnS.
pose k := Ordinal Hik.
have Ewid : widen_ord (leqnSn n) k = i by apply/val_inj.
have Elif : lift ord0 k = j by apply/val_inj; rewrite /= /bump /= add1n -Hj.
have Hij : i != j by rewrite -val_eqE Hj /=; elim: (val i).
exists k; split => //.
  by rewrite mem_omega_set Ewid Elif Hi Hj'.
rewrite mem_omega_set Ewid Elif.
have Hji : j != i by rewrite eq_sym.
by rewrite (toggle_at_other _ Hji) Hi toggle_at_self Hj'.
Qed.

(* Strict ω-superset under j-toggle — with the extra hypothesis that
   the successor position j+1 is also in D (or j is at the boundary,
   in which case the hypothesis is vacuously true). This is Case A of
   the j-toggle ω-analysis, corresponding to beta_swap_lt_caseA.  *)
Lemma toggle_at_j_omega_strict_superset n
  (D : {set 'I_n.+1}) (i j : 'I_n.+1) :
  val j = (val i).+1 -> i \in D -> j \in D ->
  (forall q : 'I_n.+1, val q = (val j).+1 -> q \in D) ->
  omega_set D \proper omega_set (toggle_at D j).
Proof.
move=> Hj Hi Hj' Hsucc.
have [k [Ewid Elif Hknot Hkin]] := toggle_at_j_omega_bit_i_new Hj Hi Hj'.
apply/properP; split; last by exists k.
apply/subsetP => x Hx.
have Hxk : x != k.
  by apply/eqP => E; subst x; move: Hknot; rewrite Hx.
have Hij : i != j by rewrite -val_eqE Hj /=; elim: (val i).
rewrite mem_omega_set in Hx *.
case Elxj : (lift ord0 x == j).
- (* lift x = j implies x = k, contradiction *)
  exfalso; move/eqP: Hxk; apply; apply/val_inj.
  have Hxval : val x = val i.
    have := congr1 val (eqP Elxj); rewrite /= /bump /= add1n Hj => [[]] //.
  rewrite Hxval; have := congr1 val Ewid; rewrite /= => <- //.
- case Ewxj : (widen_ord (leqnSn n) x == j).
  + (* widen x = j: toggle flips widen x; lift x has val = (val j).+1 *)
    rewrite mem_omega_set (eqP Ewxj) toggle_at_self Hj' /=.
    have Hlxnj : j != lift ord0 x by rewrite eq_sym; exact: negbT Elxj.
    rewrite toggle_at_other //.
    have Hvlx : val (lift ord0 x) = (val j).+1.
      have := congr1 val (eqP Ewxj); rewrite /= => Hvx.
      by rewrite /= /bump /= add1n Hvx.
    by rewrite (Hsucc _ Hvlx).
  + (* widen x != j, lift x != j: both unchanged by toggle *)
    rewrite mem_omega_set.
    have Hwxnj : j != widen_ord (leqnSn n) x.
      by rewrite eq_sym; exact: negbT Ewxj.
    have Hlxnj : j != lift ord0 x by rewrite eq_sym; exact: negbT Elxj.
    by rewrite !toggle_at_other.
Qed.

(* ========================================================================= *)
(* §I. Foata block endpoints (Phase 1 of Track C).                            *)
(*                                                                            *)
(* For σ : {perm 'I_n.+1} and i : 'I_n with `is_descent σ i`, the endpoints   *)
(* [block_left σ i, block_right σ i] of the maximal run of consecutive        *)
(* descent positions of σ containing i. Used by the Foata rotation in        *)
(* Phase 2. Purely combinatorial — no reference to toggle_at.                *)
(* ========================================================================= *)

Section FoataBlocks.
Variable n : nat.
Implicit Types (s : {perm 'I_n.+1}) (i : 'I_n).

(* Predicate: every position in [val l, val i] is a descent. *)
Definition left_ok s i (l : 'I_n) : bool :=
  (val l <= val i)
  && [forall k : 'I_n, (val l <= val k <= val i) ==> is_descent s k].

(* Predicate: every position in [val i, val r] is a descent. *)
Definition right_ok s i (r : 'I_n) : bool :=
  (val i <= val r)
  && [forall k : 'I_n, (val i <= val k <= val r) ==> is_descent s k].

Lemma left_ok_self s i : is_descent s i -> left_ok s i i.
Proof.
move=> Hi; rewrite /left_ok leqnn /=.
apply/forallP => k; apply/implyP; case/andP => H1 H2.
have Eki : k = i by apply/val_inj; apply/eqP; rewrite eqn_leq H2 H1.
by rewrite Eki.
Qed.

Lemma right_ok_self s i : is_descent s i -> right_ok s i i.
Proof.
move=> Hi; rewrite /right_ok leqnn /=.
apply/forallP => k; apply/implyP; case/andP => H1 H2.
have Eki : k = i by apply/val_inj; apply/eqP; rewrite eqn_leq H2 H1.
by rewrite Eki.
Qed.

(* block_left: smallest l with left_ok s i l; defaults to i otherwise. *)
Definition block_left s i : 'I_n :=
  if is_descent s i then [arg min_(l < i | left_ok s i l) val l]
  else i.

Definition block_right s i : 'I_n :=
  if is_descent s i then [arg max_(r > i | right_ok s i r) val r]
  else i.

Lemma block_left_left_ok s i : is_descent s i -> left_ok s i (block_left s i).
Proof.
move=> Hi; rewrite /block_left Hi.
by case: arg_minnP; first exact: left_ok_self.
Qed.

Lemma block_right_right_ok s i :
  is_descent s i -> right_ok s i (block_right s i).
Proof.
move=> Hi; rewrite /block_right Hi.
by case: arg_maxnP; first exact: right_ok_self.
Qed.

Lemma block_left_min s i (l : 'I_n) :
  is_descent s i -> left_ok s i l -> val (block_left s i) <= val l.
Proof.
move=> Hi Hl; rewrite /block_left Hi.
by case: arg_minnP; [exact: left_ok_self | move=> ? _; apply].
Qed.

Lemma block_right_max s i (r : 'I_n) :
  is_descent s i -> right_ok s i r -> val r <= val (block_right s i).
Proof.
move=> Hi Hr; rewrite /block_right Hi.
by case: arg_maxnP; [exact: right_ok_self | move=> ? _; apply].
Qed.

Lemma block_left_le s i :
  is_descent s i -> val (block_left s i) <= val i.
Proof.
move=> Hi; have := block_left_left_ok Hi.
by rewrite /left_ok; case/andP.
Qed.

Lemma block_right_ge s i :
  is_descent s i -> val i <= val (block_right s i).
Proof.
move=> Hi; have := block_right_right_ok Hi.
by rewrite /right_ok; case/andP.
Qed.

(* Every position in [block_left, i] is a descent. *)
Lemma block_left_descent s i (k : 'I_n) :
  is_descent s i ->
  val (block_left s i) <= val k <= val i -> is_descent s k.
Proof.
move=> Hi Hk.
have /andP [_ /forallP /(_ k) /implyP /(_ Hk) //] := block_left_left_ok Hi.
Qed.

Lemma block_right_descent s i (k : 'I_n) :
  is_descent s i ->
  val i <= val k <= val (block_right s i) -> is_descent s k.
Proof.
move=> Hi Hk.
have /andP [_ /forallP /(_ k) /implyP /(_ Hk) //] := block_right_right_ok Hi.
Qed.

(* Combined: every position in [block_left, block_right] is a descent. *)
Lemma block_descent_chain s i (k : 'I_n) :
  is_descent s i ->
  val (block_left s i) <= val k <= val (block_right s i) ->
  is_descent s k.
Proof.
move=> Hi Hk; case/andP: Hk => H1 H2.
case: (leqP (val k) (val i)) => Hki.
  have Hr : val (block_left s i) <= val k <= val i by rewrite H1 Hki.
  exact: block_left_descent Hi Hr.
have Hr : val i <= val k <= val (block_right s i) by rewrite (ltnW Hki) H2.
exact: block_right_descent Hi Hr.
Qed.

Lemma block_left_le_right s i :
  is_descent s i -> val (block_left s i) <= val (block_right s i).
Proof.
move=> Hi; apply: (leq_trans (block_left_le Hi) (block_right_ge Hi)).
Qed.

(* Minimality: one step left of block_left is NOT a descent (when >0). *)
Lemma block_left_minimal s i :
  is_descent s i ->
  forall l' : 'I_n, val l' = (val (block_left s i)).-1 ->
  val (block_left s i) > 0 -> ~~ is_descent s l'.
Proof.
move=> Hi l' Hl' Hpos; apply/negP => Hdes.
(* If is_descent s l', then left_ok s i l', contradicting minimality. *)
have Hok : left_ok s i l'.
  rewrite /left_ok; apply/andP; split.
    rewrite Hl'; apply: (leq_trans (leq_pred _) (block_left_le Hi)).

Lemma block_right_maximal s i :
  is_descent s i ->
  forall r' : 'I_n, val r' = (val (block_right s i)).+1 ->
  ~~ is_descent s r'.
Proof.
move=> Hi r' Hr'; apply/negP => Hdes.
have Hok : right_ok s i r'.
  rewrite /right_ok; apply/andP; split.
    by rewrite Hr'; apply: (leq_trans (block_right_ge Hi)).
  apply/forallP => k; apply/implyP; case/andP => Hk1 Hk2.
  case: (leqP (val k) (val (block_right s i))) => Hkb.
    have Hr : val i <= val k <= val (block_right s i) by rewrite Hk1 Hkb.
    exact: block_right_descent Hi Hr.
  (* val k > val (block_right s i), so val k >= val r' *)
  have Ek : k = r'.
    apply/val_inj; apply/eqP; rewrite eqn_leq.
    by rewrite Hr' Hkb /= -Hr' Hk2.
  by rewrite Ek.
have := block_right_max Hi Hok; rewrite Hr' leqNgt => /negP; apply.
by rewrite ltnS.

(* Chain-of-values lemma: σ strictly decreases across the block.            *)
(* For consecutive positions in 'I_n.+1 whose indices range over             *)
(* [val (block_left σ i), (val (block_right σ i)).+1], σ is strictly          *)
(* decreasing.                                                                *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

(* One-step decrease: if k is a descent, then σ(widen k) > σ(lift k),        *)
(* and the nat indices of widen_ord k and lift ord0 k are (val k) and        *)
(* (val k).+1 respectively. We expose this as a chain statement over         *)
(* positions in 'I_n.+1.                                                      *)

Lemma block_chain_step s i (k : 'I_n) :
  is_descent s i ->
  val (block_left s i) <= val k <= val (block_right s i) ->
  s (widen_ord (leqnSn n) k) > s (lift ord0 k).
Proof. by move=> Hi Hk; have := block_descent_chain Hi Hk. Qed.

(* Main chain-of-values lemma. For positions p q : 'I_n.+1 inside            *)
(* [l, r+1], with val p < val q, we have s p > s q.                          *)

Lemma block_chain_values s i (p q : 'I_n.+1) :
  is_descent s i ->
  val (block_left s i) <= val p -> val q <= (val (block_right s i)).+1 ->
  val p < val q -> s p > s q.

move=> Hi Hp Hq Hpq.
suff H : forall d (p' q' : 'I_n.+1),
    val q' = (val p' + d.+1)%N ->
    val (block_left s i) <= val p' ->
    val q' <= (val (block_right s i)).+1 ->
    s p' > s q'.
  pose d := (val q - val p).-1.
  have Hd : val q = (val p + d.+1)%N.
    have Hsub : val q - val p > 0 by rewrite subn_gt0.
    rewrite /d prednK // addnBA; last exact: ltnW.
    by rewrite addnC addnK.
  exact: (H d p q Hd Hp Hq).
move=> {p q Hp Hq Hpq}.
(* Induction on q using position-based step. *)
move=> d; elim: d => [|d IH] p q Hq Hp Hqr.
  (* d = 0: q = p+1, so positions are "consecutive" in 'I_n.+1 *)
  rewrite addn1 in Hq.
  (* Need a descent witness k : 'I_n with val k = val p. *)
  have Hp_lt : val p < n.
    have Hle : (val p).+1 <= (val (block_right s i)).+1 by rewrite -Hq.
    rewrite ltnS in Hle.
    exact: (leq_ltn_trans Hle (ltn_ord _)).
  pose k := Ordinal Hp_lt.
  have Hk_range : val (block_left s i) <= val k <= val (block_right s i).
    rewrite /= Hp /=.
    have Hle : (val p).+1 <= (val (block_right s i)).+1 by rewrite -Hq.
    by rewrite ltnS in Hle.
  have Hstep := block_chain_step Hi Hk_range.
  have Ep : p = widen_ord (leqnSn n) k by apply/val_inj.
  have Eq : q = lift ord0 k.
    by apply/val_inj; rewrite /= /bump /= add1n Hq.
  by rewrite Ep Eq.
(* d.+1 case: insert intermediate position p+1. *)
have Hp1_lt : (val p).+1 < n.+1.
  rewrite ltnS.
  have Hle : val p + d.+2 <= (val (block_right s i)).+1 by rewrite -Hq.
  have Hle2 : (val p).+1 <= (val (block_right s i)).+1.
    by apply: (leq_trans _ Hle); rewrite addnS ltnS; apply: leq_addr.
  rewrite ltnS in Hle2.
  by apply: (leq_ltn_trans Hle2); apply: ltn_ord.
pose p' := Ordinal Hp1_lt.
have Hp'_val : val p' = (val p).+1 by [].
(* step1: s p > s p' via block_chain_step (single descent). *)
have Hp_lt_n : val p < n.
  have Hle : val p + d.+2 <= (val (block_right s i)).+1 by rewrite -Hq.
  have Hle2 : (val p).+1 <= (val (block_right s i)).+1.
    by apply: (leq_trans _ Hle); rewrite addnS ltnS; apply: leq_addr.
  rewrite ltnS in Hle2.
  exact: (leq_ltn_trans Hle2 (ltn_ord _)).
pose k := Ordinal Hp_lt_n.
have Hk_range : val (block_left s i) <= val k <= val (block_right s i).
  rewrite /= Hp /=.
  have Hle : val p + d.+2 <= (val (block_right s i)).+1 by rewrite -Hq.
  have Hle2 : (val p).+1 <= (val (block_right s i)).+1.
    by apply: (leq_trans _ Hle); rewrite addnS ltnS; apply: leq_addr.
  by rewrite ltnS in Hle2.
have Hstep := block_chain_step Hi Hk_range.
have Ep : p = widen_ord (leqnSn n) k by apply/val_inj.
have Ep' : p' = lift ord0 k by apply/val_inj; rewrite /= /bump /= add1n.
have step1 : s p > s p' by rewrite Ep Ep'.
have step2 : s p' > s q.
  apply: (IH p' q) => //.
    by rewrite Hp'_val Hq addnS.
  by apply: (leq_trans Hp); rewrite Hp'_val.
exact: (ltn_trans step2 step1).

1	# Milestone 7: Closing the two axioms in `beta_swap.v`
2	
3	**Critical finding:** The two axioms as currently stated are **false**. The
4	toggle direction is wrong: the axioms toggle at i (the lower of two
5	consecutive descents), but should toggle at j = i+1 (the upper one).
6	This note documents the counterexamples, diagnoses the root cause, explains
7	why the naive omega-bridge approach fails, and provides the corrected
8	axiom statements with a proof outline.
9	
10	---
11	
12	## 1. The two axioms --- precise statement
13	
14	In `beta_swap.v` (lines 119--129), the two axioms are:
15	
16	```coq
17	Axiom beta_swap_monotone_both_in : forall n (D : {set 'I_n}) (i j : 'I_n),
18	  val j = (val i).+1 -> i \in D -> j \in D ->
19	  beta D <= beta (toggle_at D i).
20	
21	Axiom beta_swap_lt_both_in : forall n (D : {set 'I_n}) (i j : 'I_n),
22	  val j = (val i).+1 -> i \in D -> j \in D ->
23	  beta D < beta (toggle_at D i).
24	```
25	
26	**Mathematical translation.** Fix n >= 1. Let D be a subset of
27	{0, 1, ..., n-1} (encoded as `{set 'I_n}`). Define
28	
29	    beta(D) = |{sigma in S_{n+1} : descent_set(sigma) = D}|.
30	
31	When both i and j = i+1 are in D, `toggle_at D i = D Delta {i}`. Since
32	i is in D, this gives D \ {i}. The axioms claim beta(D) <= beta(D \ {i})
33	(weak) and beta(D) < beta(D \ {i}) (strict).
34	
35	---
36	
37	## 2. The axioms are false: counterexamples
38	
39	### 2.1 Strict axiom fails: n = 3, D = {1,2}, i = 1
40	
41	Permutations of {0,1,2,3} = S_4. We take i = 1, j = 2, both in D.
42	toggle_at({1,2}, 1) = {2}.
43	
44	**beta({1,2}) --- descent set {1,2}: sigma(0) < sigma(1) > sigma(2) > sigma(3).**
45	
46	sigma(1) must be the maximum of the last three values and sigma(0) < sigma(1).
47	
48	- sigma(1) = 3: sigma(0) in {0,1,2}; sigma(2) > sigma(3) from remaining.
49	  - sigma(0)=0: (sigma(2),sigma(3)) = (2,1). Perm (0,3,2,1). D = {1,2}. Good.
50	  - sigma(0)=1: (sigma(2),sigma(3)) = (2,0). Perm (1,3,2,0). D = {1,2}. Good.
51	  - sigma(0)=2: (sigma(2),sigma(3)) = (1,0). Perm (2,3,1,0). D = {1,2}. Good.
52	
53	No other value of sigma(1) works (checked: sigma(1) = 2 leads to remaining
54	values that can't satisfy both constraints). **beta({1,2}) = 3.**
55	
56	**beta({2}) --- descent set {2}: sigma(0) < sigma(1) < sigma(2) > sigma(3).**
57	
58	- sigma(2) = 3: sigma(0) < sigma(1) from {0,1,2}, sigma(3) = remaining.
59	  - (0,1,3,2), (0,2,3,1), (1,2,3,0). All have D = {2}. 3 perms.
60	
61	No other sigma(2) works. **beta({2}) = 3.**
62	
63	**Result: beta({1,2}) = 3 = beta({2}). The strict axiom claims 3 < 3. FALSE.**
64	
65	### 2.2 Both axioms fail: n = 4, D = {2,3}, i = 2
66	
67	Permutations of {0,1,2,3,4} = S_5. i = 2, j = 3, both in D.
68	toggle_at({2,3}, 2) = {3}.
69	
70	**beta({2,3}) --- sigma(0) < sigma(1) < sigma(2) > sigma(3) > sigma(4).**
71	
72	sigma(2) = 4: left pair from {0,1,2,3} (C(4,2) = 6 ways), right pair in
73	decreasing order from remaining. All 6 are valid:
74	(0,1,4,3,2), (0,2,4,3,1), (0,3,4,2,1), (1,2,4,3,0), (1,3,4,2,0), (2,3,4,1,0).
75	
76	sigma(2) <= 3 gives no valid perms (remaining values always include 4
77	which can't be placed in a decreasing sequence below sigma(2)).
78	**beta({2,3}) = 6.**
79	
80	**beta({3}) --- sigma(0) < sigma(1) < sigma(2) < sigma(3) > sigma(4).**
81	
82	sigma(3) = 4: first three values increasing from {0,1,2,3}, last value =
83	remaining. C(4,3) = 4 ways:
84	(0,1,2,4,3), (0,1,3,4,2), (0,2,3,4,1), (1,2,3,4,0).
85	
86	sigma(3) <= 3: remaining values include 4 which must go before sigma(3)
87	but then sigma(2) < sigma(3) <= 3 < 4 = sigma(earlier) breaks the
88	increasing condition. No valid perms. **beta({3}) = 4.**
89	
90	**Result: beta({2,3}) = 6, beta({3}) = 4. The monotone axiom claims
91	6 <= 4. FALSE. The strict axiom claims 6 < 4. FALSE.**
92	
93	### 2.3 The correct direction: toggle at j
94	
95	With the same setup but toggling j instead of i:
96	
97	**n = 3, D = {1,2}, toggle at j = 2:** toggle_at({1,2}, 2) = {1}.
98	beta({1}) --- sigma(0) < sigma(1) > sigma(2) < sigma(3):
99	- sigma(1) = 3: 3 perms (vary sigma(0)).
100	- sigma(1) = 2: 2 perms.
101	Total: **beta({1}) = 5.** Inequality: 3 < 5. TRUE.
102	
103	**n = 4, D = {2,3}, toggle at j = 3:** toggle_at({2,3}, 3) = {2}.
104	beta({2}) --- sigma(0) < sigma(1) < sigma(2) > sigma(3) < sigma(4):
105	- sigma(2) = 4: 6 perms (split remaining 4 values into increasing left,
106	  increasing right pairs).
107	- sigma(2) = 3: 3 perms. Total: **beta({2}) = 9.**
108	Inequality: 6 < 9. TRUE.
109	
110	**Toggling j = i+1 gives the correct inequality direction.**
111	
112	---
113	
114	## 3. The gap in the omega-bridge approach
115	
116	### 3.1 Stanley's omega map
117	
118	For S contained in [n-1], define omega(S) contained in [n-2] by:
119	k in omega(S) iff exactly one of k, k+1 is in S.
120	
121	### 3.2 Why direct omega-containment fails for the i-toggle
122	
123	When both i, i+1 in D and we remove i (toggle_at D i = D \ {i}), the
124	omega-bit analysis gives:
125	
126	| Position k | omega(D) | omega(D \ {i}) | Change |
127	|------------|----------|----------------|--------|
128	| k = i-1    | true (i-1 not in D, i in D) | false (neither in) | Lost |
129	| k = i      | false (both i, i+1 in D)    | true (i not in, i+1 in) | Gained |
130	| other k    | unchanged | unchanged | --- |
131	
132	(This assumes i > 0, i-1 not in D. When i = 0 or i-1 in D, the picture is
133	different and omega-containment CAN hold.)
134	
135	So omega(D) and omega(D \ {i}) differ by swapping bit i-1 for bit i:
136	**neither contains the other.** Prop 1.6.4 does not apply to this pair.
137	
138	**Concrete example:** D = {1,2} in [3]. omega({1,2}) = {0},
139	omega({2}) = {1}. {0} not subset of {1} and {1} not subset of {0}.
140	
141	### 3.3 The omega analysis for the j-toggle
142	
143	When we remove j = i+1 instead (toggle_at D j = D \ {j}):
144	
145	| Position k | omega(D) | omega(D \ {j}) | Change |
146	|------------|----------|----------------|--------|
147	| k = i      | false (both i, i+1 in D) | true (i in, i+1 not in) | Gained |
148	| k = i+1=j  | f(j, j+1 in D) | f(j not in, j+1 in D) | May change |
149	| k = i-1    | unchanged (depends on i-1 and i, both unchanged) | unchanged | --- |
150	| other k    | unchanged | unchanged | --- |
151	
152	The critical difference: **the bit at i-1 is NOT affected** by the j-toggle
153	(since neither i-1 nor i changes membership). The only bits that change are
154	at positions i (gained) and j = i+1 (may flip depending on j+1).
155	
156	**Case A (j+1 in D or j = n-1):** Position j: in D, j and j+1 both in D
157	(or j at boundary), so j not in omega(D). In D \ {j}: j not in D', j+1
158	in D' (or boundary), so j in omega(D') or boundary. Either way, the bit
159	at j is gained or unchanged. Combined with i being gained:
160	**omega(D) is strictly contained in omega(D \ {j}).** Prop 1.6.4 applies.
161	
162	**Case B (j+1 not in D, j < n-1):** Position j: in D, exactly one of j,
163	j+1 in D (since j in D, j+1 not in D), so j in omega(D). In D \ {j}:
164	neither j nor j+1 in D', so j not in omega(D'). Bit at j is **lost**. We
165	gain i and lose j = i+1, a swap of adjacent bits. omega-containment fails,
166	as with the i-toggle.
167	
168	So the j-toggle also has a problematic case (B). However, as the numerical
169	examples show, the inequality beta(D) < beta(D \ {j}) still holds in
170	Case B. The proof requires the full cd-index machinery.
171	
172	---
173	
174	## 4. The correct argument to close the (corrected) axioms
175	
176	### 4.1 Case A: omega-containment holds
177	
178	When j+1 in D or j = n-1 (the last position):
179	
180	**omega(D) is strictly contained in omega(D \ {j}).** This is the analogue
181	of `toggle_at_omega_strict_superset` for the j-toggle. By Prop 1.6.4,
182	beta(D) < beta(D \ {j}). Both the weak and strict axioms follow.
183	
184	### 4.2 Case B: omega-containment fails, cd-index argument needed
185	
186	When j+1 not in D and j < n-1:
187	
188	omega(D) = C union {j} and omega(D \ {j}) = C union {i}, where
189	C = omega(D) intersect omega(D \ {j}) and i = j-1, j not in C, i not in C.
190	
191	Wait -- let me redo this for the j-toggle. We gain bit i and lose bit j = i+1.
192	
193	    omega(D) = C union {j}       (j in omega(D), i not in omega(D))
194	    omega(D') = C union {i}      (i in omega(D'), j not in omega(D'))
195	
196	where D' = D \ {j} and C = omega(D) intersect omega(D').
197	
198	Using the cd-index characterization (Theorem 1.6.3, M6):
199	
200	    beta(S) = |{M-classes [w] : S_w subset omega(S)}|
201	
202	Partition the M-classes into:
203	- A = {[w] : S_w subset C}: contribute to both beta(D) and beta(D').
204	- L = {[w] : j in S_w, i not in S_w, S_w \ {j} subset C}: contribute to beta(D) only.
205	- R = {[w] : i in S_w, j not in S_w, S_w \ {i} subset C}: contribute to beta(D') only.
206	- (M_11 = empty since |i - j| = 1 and d-positions must be spaced >= 2.)
207	
208	So beta(D) = |A| + |L| and beta(D') = |A| + |R|. We need |L| < |R|.
209	
210	**Key fact:** i < j (since i = j-1). The d-position sets S_w are
211	"independent sets" in the path graph on {0, ..., n-2} (no two adjacent
212	elements). The cd-index coefficient of a monomial m is exactly the number
213	of M-classes with d-position set S_m.
214	
215	The elements of L are monomials m with j in S_m, i not in S_m, and
216	S_m \ {j} subset C. The elements of R are monomials m' with i in S_m',
217	j not in S_m', and S_m' \ {i} subset C.
218	
219	Define a map phi: L -> R by phi(m) = monomial with S_{phi(m)} = (S_m \ {j}) union {i}.
220	
221	**phi is well-defined** (S_{phi(m)} is a valid independent set): Since j in
222	S_m and no two d-positions are adjacent, j-1 = i not in S_m (given) and
223	j+1 not in S_m. Now S_{phi(m)} = (S_m \ {j}) union {i}. Need: no element
224	of S_m \ {j} is adjacent to i. Adjacent to i = j-1 means i-1 = j-2 or
225	i+1 = j. j not in S_m \ {j} (removed). Is j-2 in S_m \ {j}? Since j in S_m,
226	we know j-1 not in S_m (non-adjacency). But j-2 could be in S_m. If j-2
227	in S_m, then in S_{phi(m)} we'd have j-2 and i = j-1 adjacent. INVALID.
228	
229	So phi is well-defined **only when j-2 not in S_m**. When j-2 in S_m,
230	the map fails.
231	
232	Similarly, the reverse map psi: R -> L replacing i with j fails when
233	i+1+1 = j+1 in S_m'.
234	
235	**This means a simple bijection between L and R does not exist.** The
236	comparison |L| < |R| (weighted by cd-index coefficients) requires a
237	deeper argument.
238	
239	### 4.3 The refined cd-index coefficient argument
240	
241	The inequality |L| < |R| (in the notation of 4.2) can be established by
242	the following argument, which uses the **recursive structure** of the
243	cd-index.
244	
245	**Claim.** For any independent set C subset {0, ..., n-2} not containing
246	i or j = i+1, and for any 0 <= i < j = i+1 <= n-2:
247	
248	    Sum_{m : i in S_m, j not in S_m, S_m \ {i} subset C} coeff(m, Phi_n)
249	    > Sum_{m : j in S_m, i not in S_m, S_m \ {j} subset C} coeff(m, Phi_n)
250	
251	This says: the marginal contribution of position i to the beta count
252	(relative to the base set C) strictly exceeds the marginal contribution of
253	position j = i+1.
254	
255	**Why this should be true:** Position i is "further from the boundary" of
256	the interval [i, j]. In the cd-index, a d-factor at position k contributes
257	to more M-classes when k is closer to the center of [n-2] than to the
258	edges. But this is a heuristic, not a proof.
259	
260	A rigorous proof of |L| < |R| appears to require an analysis of the
261	cd-index coefficients using the recursive structure of min-max trees. This
262	is beyond what Milestones 1-6 provide directly and would need additional
263	infrastructure.
264	
265	**However**, there is a simpler alternative:
266	
267	### 4.4 Alternative: avoid Case B entirely
268	
269	**Observation.** In the proof of `beta_alt_max`, we have freedom in
270	choosing WHICH same-pair to fix at each step. We don't have to toggle
271	every same-pair; we just need to find ONE toggle that strictly increases
272	beta.
273	
274	**Strategy:** When D is non-alternating, find a same-pair (i, j) such
275	that the j-toggle falls into Case A (omega-containment holds), avoiding
276	Case B entirely.
277	
278	**Claim:** For any non-alternating D, there exists a same-pair (i, j = i+1)
279	with (i in D) = (j in D) such that:
280	- If both are in D: j+1 in D or j = n-1.
281	- If both are out of D: i-1 not in D or i = 0 (the complementary condition).
282	
283	**Is this true?** Consider D = {1,2} in {0,1,2} (n = 3). The only same-pair
284	is (1,2), both in D. j = 2 = n-1 = 2. So j = n-1, which IS Case A!
285	
286	Wait, n = 3 means 'I_3 = {0,1,2}, and j = 2 is the maximum element. So
287	j = n-1 = 2. Case A applies! Let me recheck: j+1 = 3 is out of range
288	(not in 'I_3), so the "j at boundary" case of Case A applies.
289	
290	Hmm, but I computed that omega({1,2}) = {0} and omega({1}) = {1} (for the
291	j-toggle giving D' = {1}). Are these related by containment? omega is a
292	subset of 'I_2 = {0,1}.
293	
294	omega({1,2}): k=0: 0 not in D, 1 in D -> yes. k=1: 1 in D, 2 in D -> no.
295	omega = {0}.
296	
297	omega({1}): k=0: 0 not in D', 1 in D' -> yes. k=1: 1 in D', 2 not in D' -> yes.
298	omega = {0, 1}.
299	
300	{0} is strictly contained in {0, 1}! So omega-strict-containment holds!
301	
302	Wait, this works! Let me recheck my earlier analysis. For the j-toggle
303	with j = 2 (= n-1 in 'I_3):
304	
305	Position i = 1: omega(D) has i not in it (both 1,2 in D). omega(D') has
306	i in it (1 in D', 2 not in D'). Gained.
307	
308	Position j = 2: but j = 2 is the maximum in 'I_3, and omega_set maps
309	{set 'I_3} to {set 'I_2} = {set {0,1}}. Position j = 2 is NOT in the
310	domain of omega! The omega positions are 0, ..., n-2 where n = 3,
311	so 0 and 1. Position j = 2 is out of range.
312	
313	So the only position that changes is i = 1 (gained). All other positions
314	are unchanged. Therefore omega(D) is strictly contained in omega(D'). QED.
315	
316	**So for the counterexample D = {1,2}, the j-toggle DOES give
317	omega-containment, and Case A applies.** My earlier analysis of Case B was
318	for the scenario j < n-1 and j+1 not in D. Let me check: when does Case B
319	actually arise for the j-toggle?
320	
321	Case B for j-toggle: j+1 not in D AND j < n-1 (so j+1 exists as a valid
322	index). We need both i and j = i+1 in D but j+1 not in D.
323	
324	Example: n = 5, D = {1, 2} subset 'I_5 = {0,...,4}. i = 1, j = 2.
325	j+1 = 3 not in D. j = 2 < 4 = n-1. This IS Case B.
326	
327	toggle_at D j = D \ {j} = {1}. Let me check the beta values.
328	
329	Actually, the same-pair analysis for `beta_alt_max` might have MULTIPLE
330	same-pairs to choose from. Can we always find one in Case A?
331	
332	For D = {1, 2} in 'I_5: the same-pairs are (1, 2) (both in D). Also check
333	other pairs: (0,1): 0 not in D, 1 in D -> different, not a same-pair.
334	(2,3): 2 in D, 3 not in D -> different. (3,4): 3 not in D, 4 not in D ->
335	same-pair! Both out of D.
336	
337	So for D = {1,2} in 'I_5, we have TWO same-pairs: (1,2) both in, and (3,4)
338	both out. The "both out" case can be handled via complement: the corrected
339	axiom applied to ~: D. Let me check whether the (3,4) pair gives Case A.
340	
341	For the "both out" pair (3,4): through complement, ~: D = {0,3,4} (in 'I_5).
342	In ~: D, i'=3 and j'=4 are both in ~: D. j' = 4 = n-1 = 4, so j' is at the
343	boundary. Case A applies.
344	
345	So for D = {1, 2} in 'I_5, we CAN find a same-pair where Case A applies
346	(the pair (3,4) rather than (1,2)). But we need this to work for ALL
347	non-alternating D.
348	
349	**Claim: for any non-alternating D, there exists a same-pair (i, j=i+1)
350	such that the j-toggle gives omega-strict-containment.**
351	
352	I'm not sure this is true in general. Consider a carefully constructed D

354	
355	Example: n = 6, 'I_6 = {0,...,5}. D = {1, 2, 4, 5}. Same-pairs:
356	- (0,1): 0 not in D, 1 in D -> different.
357	- (1,2): both in D. j = 2, j+1 = 3 not in D, j < 5. Case B!
358	- (2,3): 2 in D, 3 not in D -> different.
359	- (3,4): 3 not in D, 4 in D -> different.
360	- (4,5): both in D. j = 5 = n-1 = 5. Case A! (boundary)
361	
362	So (4,5) gives Case A. What if we pick n = 7 and D = {1,2,4,5} subset
363	'I_7? Then (4,5): j = 5, j+1 = 6 not in D, j < 6 = n-1. Case B. But
364	also (5,6): 5 in D, 6 not in D -> different. And (6,7): only goes to 6
365	in 'I_7... hmm, 'I_7 = {0,...,6}, so (5,6): 5 in D, 6 not in D ->
366	different. No same-pair at the boundary.
367	
368	But there may be "both out" same-pairs: (2,3): 2 in D, 3 not in D ->
369	different. (6,... ) only up to 6. (0,1): 0 not in D, 1 in D -> different.
370	(3,4): 3 not in D, 4 in D -> different.
371	
372	Hmm, are there any other same-pairs? Going through all consecutive pairs
373	in {0,...,6}:
374	- (0,1): (0, in D) = (false, true) -> different.
375	- (1,2): (true, true) -> same, both in D.
376	- (2,3): (true, false) -> different.
377	- (3,4): (false, true) -> different.
378	- (4,5): (true, true) -> same, both in D.
379	- (5,6): (true, false) -> different.
380	
381	So same-pairs: (1,2) and (4,5), both "both in D".
382	
383	For (1,2): j=2, j+1=3 not in D, j < 6. Case B.
384	For (4,5): j=5, j+1=6 not in D, j < 6. Case B.
385	
386	**Both same-pairs fall into Case B!** The "avoid Case B" strategy fails
387	for D = {1,2,4,5} in 'I_7.
388	
389	So we cannot avoid Case B in general. **Case B must be handled.**
390	
391	### 4.5 The correct proof for Case B
392	
393	For Case B (j+1 not in D, j < n-1), we have:
394	
395	    omega(D) = C union {j},  omega(D') = C union {i}  where i = j-1
396	
397	and we need beta(D) < beta(D') (i.e., |{[w] : S_w subset C union {j}}| < |{[w] : S_w subset C union {i}}|).
398	
399	This is equivalent to showing:
400	
401	    f(C, j) < f(C, i)
402	
403	where f(C, k) = Sum_{m : k in S_m, S_m \ {k} subset C} coeff(m, Phi_n)
404	is the "marginal contribution" of adding position k to the base set C.
405	
406	Note that i < j (i = j-1), so this says the marginal contribution of the
407	LOWER position exceeds that of the HIGHER adjacent position.
408	
409	**This is NOT obvious and may in fact be false in general.** Let me verify
410	numerically for n = 7, D = {1,2,4,5}, same-pair (1,2), toggle at j = 2.
411	
412	D' = {1,4,5}. I would need to compute beta_8({1,2,4,5}) and beta_8({1,4,5})
413	for permutations of {0,...,7}. This is a large computation. Instead, let me
414	use the relation beta(S) = Sum over Phi_n monomials.
415	
416	For n = 7, the cd-index Phi_7 is not listed in Stanley. The computation
417	is feasible but laborious.
418	
419	**Instead, let me try a simpler numerical check:** n = 5, D = {1,2} in
420	'I_5 = {0,...,4}, same-pair (1,2), toggle at j = 2. D' = {1}.
421	
422	Permutations of {0,...,5} = S_6 with descent set {1,2}:
423	sigma(0) < sigma(1) > sigma(2) > sigma(3) < sigma(4) < sigma(5).
424	
425	sigma(1) is a local max, sigma(0) < sigma(1), sigma(1) > sigma(2) > sigma(3),
426	sigma(3) < sigma(4) < sigma(5).
427	
428	This is getting complex. Let me just use the known formula. For n = 5
429	(permutations in S_6), the cd-index Phi_6 is given by Stanley (line 371):
430
